cards.front: A lower motor lesion of which cranial nerve makes the protruded tongue deviate toward the weak side? [___]
cards.context: The intact genioglossus pushes the tongue toward the side of weakness. This is a functional consequence of asymmetric tongue force, not a sensory deficit.

cards.front: Which gluteal muscle powerfully extends the hip when rising? [___]
cards.context: It is recruited when rising from a chair or climbing. Its large size reflects the force required to extend the hip against body weight.

cards.front: A peripheral palsy of which cranial nerve weakens the upper and lower ipsilateral face? [___]
cards.context: A peripheral lesion affects upper and lower facial muscles on one side. This differs from a typical supranuclear lesion, which often spares the forehead.
